key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than reduce reflection—they also improve wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and potentially mechanical stability.
engineering_relevance: Texturing is a multi-functional design strategy that can raise efficiency and reliability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Review of recently reported texture-enabled benefits beyond light management
Focus on wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and mechanical robustness
Synthesizes implications for solar cells, photodetectors, and LEDs
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature survey of recent reports rather than a single new experiment, highlighting recurring texture-related improvements across multiple studies.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on processing, geometry, and device stack, so gains in one platform may not transfer directly to another.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
